product.title: Deploy your SaaS into customer AWS
product.intro: Deployz helps small SaaS teams prepare, install, and update supported apps in their customers' AWS accounts.
sections: Check the app
Connect GitHub with read-only access. Review the readiness report, provide settings, and fix relevant code blockers. Build a release and test it in your own AWS account.
Get customer approval
Send an installation link. The customer reviews resources, estimated AWS costs, and requested permissions. They approve the connector in their AWS console. They do not need a Deployz account.
Manage customer releases
Select a release for each customer. Start updates and check deployment status. Rollbacks do not reverse database migrations.
product.fit: One Linux x86-64 image with an HTTP service. Optional workers use the same image. Supported data services include PostgreSQL 16 or MySQL 8.0, Redis-compatible cache, and S3. Deployz creates a new VPC.

AWS costs are separate.

security.title: Deployment architecture and access
security.intro: For customer technical reviewers. Deployz coordinates supported deployments through a connector that the customer approves in their AWS account.
sections: Connection
The customer reviews the requested IAM actions and creates a CloudFormation connector stack. The connector calls out to Deployz. Deployz does not make an inbound connection to it.
Approved resource changes
The connector can create a dedicated VPC, load balancer, security groups, ECS services, supported data services, and application IAM roles. It can read and write secrets tagged for the installation.
Permission limits

Most write actions are limited to installation resources. The connector role has a permissions boundary. The CloudFormation role that creates app resources does not. Each IAM role that it creates must carry an application role boundary.
Responsibilities

Deployz manages supported infrastructure and deployment operations. The SaaS vendor manages code, configuration, integrations, and data handling. The customer manages its AWS account, access, billing, and governance.

security.title: Data paths and service dependencies
security.intro: Customer AWS hosting is one part of the data flow. Review application integrations and all external services before making data handling commitments.
sections: Deployment metadata
Deployz receives installation and AWS account IDs, Region, versions, deployment state, resource IDs, AWS error messages, and health-check results.
Application data
The connector does not send database data, cache contents, S3 data, application logs, or in-memory app data to Deployz. The connector cannot read application logs.
Code and secrets

Repository access is read-only. Builds and the image registry run in Deployz's AWS account. AI may read redacted repository excerpts. Secrets stay encrypted before delivery to customer Secrets Manager. Values shared across customers remain encrypted in Deployz.
Request routing

Traffic to the default deployz.dev app URL passes through the Deployz proxy on Cloudflare. A custom domain routes directly to the customer's load balancer. Model APIs and other integrations can receive data from the app.

security.title: Operations and customer review
security.intro: Use these checks before customer approval. This brief describes the product. It is not an audit report, a contract, or a guarantee of compliance.
sections: Updates and rollback
The vendor starts each update. If a new version fails its health check, the previous version keeps running. Rollbacks do not reverse database migrations.
Service interruption

If Deployz is unavailable, existing apps can keep running. New installations and updates pause. New tasks need the Deployz image registry. The default app URL needs the proxy. A custom domain does not use that proxy.
Removal and access

Removal keeps the database, its credentials, and the S3 bucket. These can continue to cause AWS charges. Data deletion is a separate confirmed step. Remove the deployment before deleting the connector stack, which ends Deployz access.
Assurance and checks

Deployz has not completed its own SOC 2 audit. Provider reports cover provider controls only. Review requested IAM actions, application data flows, migrations, retained resources, and the customer's own AWS requirements.

faq: Will Deployz work with our app?
It supports one Linux x86-64 container image and an HTTP service. Workers must use the same image. Review database and storage needs in the readiness report. Some apps need code changes.
Can we use an existing VPC?
The current supported architecture creates a new dedicated VPC. Existing customer VPCs are not supported.
What is outside the current scope?
Other clouds, on-premises systems, Kubernetes, serverless apps, GPUs, ARM64 images, separate service images, Kafka, RabbitMQ, and attachable disk volumes are not supported.
Does the customer need a Deployz account?
No. The customer opens the installation link, verifies email, reviews the request, and approves the connector in AWS.
What does the free evaluation include?
Readiness analysis, configuration, release builds, and one active test deployment per application in your own AWS account. No card or time limit. AWS resource charges still apply.
What do we pay?

The paid plan is USD 49/month plus USD 19 per billable customer environment/month. Subscriptions start at USD 68/month and always include at least one billable customer environment. AWS bills the AWS account owner separately.
When is a customer environment billable?

Billing starts when it first becomes ready. Billing pauses if it has failed with nothing running, or its connector has not checked in for 15 minutes. A failed update with the old release still running remains billable. Check the pricing page for full rules. A subscription always bills at least one customer environment.
Does AI change our code or create infrastructure?
Repository access is read-only. AI-assisted analysis can provide fix instructions. Your team changes the code. The rule-based compiler creates supported infrastructure through the connector.
Does all data stay in customer AWS?

Review each data path. App resources run in customer AWS. Deployz receives deployment metadata, builds images in its account, and handles secrets as described in the security brief. App integrations can send data externally.
Is Deployz SOC 2 certified?
Deployz has not completed its own SOC 2 audit. Customer hosting on AWS does not by itself make an app secure or compliant.
What happens after a failed update?
If the new version fails its health check, the previous version keeps running. A rollback does not reverse database migrations. Plan database compatibility before release.
What happens if we cancel?
Existing customer environments keep running. You can still update, roll back, and remove them. You cannot start new customer deployments until the subscription is active again.
Can we stop using Deployz?
The app uses standard AWS services. Your team takes responsibility for future deployment operations. Default app URLs depend on the proxy, and new tasks pull images from the Deployz registry.
What remains after removal?
The database, its credentials, and the S3 bucket remain. They can continue to cause AWS charges. Delete retained data as a separate confirmed action.
Can you promise a deployment time or savings?
No measured time or savings claim is included in this material. Start with readiness analysis and a test deployment for your app.

evaluation.title: App readiness and test checklist
evaluation.intro: For the SaaS vendor. Use a test AWS account first. Free evaluation does not remove AWS resource charges.
items: Confirm one Linux x86-64 image and an HTTP endpoint.
Confirm workers use the same image and supported data services.
Confirm the customer accepts a new VPC in AWS.
Identify model APIs and other external data flows.
Connect GitHub and review repository permissions.
Review the readiness report and all relevant blockers.
Provide settings and secret values through the app.
Fix code issues and build a versioned release.
Review the AWS resource and cost estimate.
Approve the test connector in your own AWS account.
Check health, app functions, workers, storage, and integrations.
Record any failed checks and the changes required.
evaluation.end: Test acceptance: the intended release is ready, app functions pass, and required integrations work. Do not treat a readiness report alone as proof.

evaluation.title: Customer installation checklist
evaluation.intro: For the SaaS vendor and customer account owner. Complete technical review before approving access or making changes.
items: Confirm a successful test for the release to install.
Confirm the vendor subscription is active.
Agree who owns code, AWS access, costs, and operations.
Review the security brief and application data flows.
Plan database migrations and rollback limits.
Choose the default URL or a custom domain.
Send the customer installation link.
Customer: verify email and review resources and permissions.
Customer: approve the connector in the AWS console.
Check the release, health, HTTPS, and app functions.
Record the release owner and support contact.
Plan removal, retained data, and AWS cost review.
evaluation.end: Customer acceptance: the agreed release works in the intended AWS account. Record approval and unresolved issues in your own project records.
